Save a lightweight RNA project for meta-analysis

rna_save.Rd

Extracts the essential components from a rna_project object and saves a simplified, memory-efficient version as an .rds file. The function removes large intermediate objects (e.g., expression matrices, model objects, and plots) while preserving key results required for downstream analyses and cross-study comparisons.

This function is designed as a bridge between individual RNA-seq analyses and meta-analysis workflows (e.g., integration via metaOmicsR).

Usage

rna_save(project, file, compress = "xz", verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

project

A rna_project object generated through the standard workflow (rna_project(), rna_import(), rna_normalize(), rna_compare(), etc.).

file

Character. Output file path where the .rds object will be saved.

compress

Character. Compression method passed to saveRDS() (default: "xz").

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints a message upon successful save (default: TRUE).

Value

Invisibly returns a cleaned rna_project object containing:

study_info

General study metadata (organism, platform, sample size, gene identifier type, and contrast definition).

gene_info

Gene annotation table (gene_id, symbol, entrez).

de_results

Differential expression results with standardized column names.

enrichment

Pathway enrichment results (e.g., GSEA output).

qc

Quality control summary extracted from project logs.

version

Version of the originating rna_project.

Details

The function performs the following steps:

1. Validation
Ensures the input object is a valid rna_project.

2. Extraction of latest results
For each component (input, normalization, comparison, enrichment, QC), only the most recent analysis (identified by the "last" pointer) is retained to avoid redundancy and reduce file size.

3. Contrast parsing
The comparison contrast is parsed to extract:

  • condition_tested (e.g., treated, disease)

  • reference_condition (e.g., control, baseline)

This information is critical for consistent interpretation of effect directions across studies in meta-analysis.

4. Object simplification
Heavy elements such as expression matrices, model objects, and intermediate structures are removed. Only summary-level data required for integration are preserved.

5. Serialization
The cleaned object is saved as a compressed .rds file, enabling efficient storage and fast reloading in R environments.

See also

rna_project, rna_import, rna_compare, rna_gsea

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Save a processed project for meta-analysis
rna_save(project = my_project,
         file = "my_project.rds")

# Save with alternative compression
rna_save(my_project,
         file = "my_project.rds",
         compress = "gzip")
} # }
